risk_if_not_implemented: Without Cryptographic Cipher Suites and Protocols Inventory, data in transit and at rest may be exposed through weak, misconfigured or compromised cryptographic protections. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Long-Term Confidentiality Loss from Cryptographic Obsolescence (R-IP-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Harvest Now / Decrypt Later (HNDL) (MT-28), Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement (MT-31).

compensating_control_1.name: Use of Cryptographic Controls
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of cryptographic protections controls using known public standards and trusted cryptographic technologies.
compensating_control_1.justification: Use of Cryptographic Controls (CRY-02) provides cryptographic protection that compensates for the absence of Cryptographic Cipher Suites and Protocols Inventory (CRY-04) by ensuring data confidentiality and integrity through alternative technical means. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Cryptographic Key Management
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate cryptographic key management controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of keys.
compensating_control_2.justification: Cryptographic Key Management (CRY-10) provides cryptographic protection that compensates for the absence of Cryptographic Cipher Suites and Protocols Inventory (CRY-04) by ensuring data confidentiality and integrity through alternative technical means. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
